Title: Source 2: Adapted from Louisiana's Food Traditions: An Insider's Guide
Author: by Maida Owens
Content: Gumbo is a dish that is closely identified with South Louisiana. It blends African, European, and Native American cultures. The word itself is from the Bantu word for okra, nkombo. The okra plant was brought to America by Portuguese traders. Some of the spices are from the Native Americans. The origin of gumbo is often credited to the French bouillabaisse¹, but the strong preference for soups in Africa strengthened the tradition.
